name: the-devbar-hint-matches-the-sidebar-hint
description: the floating address bar's hover hint and a sidebar row's hover hint, compared for font, padding, radius, shadow and colour. hint.js's hideHint() runs at the top of every showHint(), so only one hint bubble ever exists at a time - there is no way to put both on screen in the same frame. The honest reading of 'side by side' is two captures taken under identical conditions (same fixture, same tint, same ambilight-off setting, same button label 'Back') and compared by eye, not a single frame. The sidebar's own back/forward/reload group is removed from its row while the devbar is up (setNavGroupInRow), so the sidebar hint is captured FIRST, before Cmd+Shift+D brings the devbar up for the second capture. Both hovers land on the shared .sbback button built by buildNavGroup, so the label and hotkey text are identical either way - the only thing left to differ is the bubble's own style.

actions.note: ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.sbnav .nb.sbback'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerover', {bubbles: true})); return 'hovered'; })()
actions.note: the sidebar's own back/forward/reload group is still in the row here - the devbar has not been opened yet
element-anchored, so the sidebar route sends this through chrome.send to HintOverlayWidget's own /hint document rather than rendering locally

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.dvnav .nb.sbback'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerover', {bubbles: true})); return 'hovered'; })()
